AGREEMENT BETWEEN OWNER AND ARCHITECT FOR DESIGN SERVICES

This Agreement Between Owner and Architect (this "Agreement") is made as of April 6, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Harrowgate Community Health, a Pennsylvania nonprofit corporation, with offices at 1400 Bellamy Avenue, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19146 ("Owner"), and Vessel & Roark Architects LLP, a Pennsylvania limited liability partnership, with offices at 88 Wharton Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19147 ("Architect"). Owner and Architect are each a "Party" and together the "Parties."

RECITALS

A. Owner intends to design and construct a three-story, 46,000 square foot outpatient clinic at 2210 Girard Avenue, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (the "Project").

B. Architect is licensed to practice architecture in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and has agreed to provide the design services described in this Agreement.

C. The Parties are entering into this Agreement to state the scope, schedule, compensation, and allocation of risk for those services.

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Basic Services" means the services described in Section 2.

1.2 "Additional Services" means services outside the scope of Basic Services, authorized in writing by Owner before performance under Section 3.

1.3 "Instruments of Service" means the drawings, specifications, models, and other documents, in any medium, that Architect and its consultants prepare for the Project.

1.4 "Construction Cost" means the total cost to Owner of the work designed or specified by Architect, excluding Architect's compensation, land cost, and financing cost.

2. BASIC SERVICES

2.1 Phases. Architect shall provide Basic Services in five phases: Schematic Design, Design Development, Construction Documents, Bidding and Negotiation, and Construction Administration.

2.2 Schematic Design. Architect shall prepare a schematic design that describes the scale and relationship of the Project components, together with a preliminary estimate of the Construction Cost, and shall submit it to Owner for written approval.

2.3 Design Development. Following Owner's written approval of the schematic design, Architect shall prepare design development documents fixing the size and character of the Project as to architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, and shall update the estimate of the Construction Cost.

2.4 Construction Documents. Following Owner's written approval of the design development documents, Architect shall prepare construction documents setting forth in detail the requirements for construction of the Project, and shall assist Owner in preparing bidding documents and in filing for the approvals of governmental authorities having jurisdiction.

2.5 Bidding and Negotiation. Architect shall assist Owner in obtaining and evaluating bids and in preparing the construction contract.

2.6 Construction Administration. Architect shall visit the site at intervals appropriate to the stage of construction, and not less than twice each month, to become generally familiar with the progress and quality of the work. Architect is not required to make exhaustive or continuous on-site inspections, and does not control or have charge of construction means, methods, sequences, or procedures, or of the safety precautions and programs of the contractor, which remain the contractor's sole responsibility.

2.7 Certificates for Payment. Architect shall review the contractor's applications for payment and shall issue certificates for payment in the amounts Architect determines to be properly due, based on Architect's observations at the site and on the data in the application. Issuance of a certificate for payment is not a representation that Architect has reviewed the contractor's means and methods or has examined how the contractor has used money previously paid.

3. ADDITIONAL SERVICES

Additional Services are performed only after Owner authorizes them in writing, and are compensated under Section 5.3. Architect shall notify Owner in writing before performing any service Architect believes is an Additional Service, and shall not proceed until Owner authorizes it. A change in the scope, quality, or budget of the Project requested by Owner, a change in law after the Effective Date, and a redesign required by Owner's rejection of documents that conform to a previously approved phase are each an Additional Service.

4. OWNER'S RESPONSIBILITIES

Owner shall provide a written program setting forth the objectives, schedule, and budget for the Project; shall furnish surveys, geotechnical reports, and environmental studies of the site; shall designate a representative authorized to act on Owner's behalf; and shall render decisions and approvals in a timely manner so as not to delay Architect's services. Architect is entitled to rely on the accuracy and completeness of the information Owner furnishes.

5. COMPENSATION

5.1 Basic Services Fee. Owner shall pay Architect a fixed fee of $1,240,000 for Basic Services, allocated among the phases as follows: Schematic Design, 15%; Design Development, 20%; Construction Documents, 40%; Bidding and Negotiation, 5%; and Construction Administration, 20%.

5.2 Invoicing. Architect shall invoice Owner monthly, in proportion to the services performed within each phase. Owner shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt. An undisputed amount that remains unpaid after forty-five (45) days bears interest at one percent (1%) per month.

5.3 Additional Services. Additional Services are compensated at Architect's standard hourly rates set forth in Exhibit A, which are fixed through December 31, 2026 and thereafter adjusted not more than once each year.

5.4 Reimbursable Expenses. Owner shall reimburse Architect for reproduction, permit and filing fees, authorized travel, and models and renderings Owner requests, at cost plus five percent (5%), up to $60,000 without Owner's further written authorization.

6. STANDARD OF CARE

Architect shall perform its services with the professional skill and care ordinarily provided by architects practicing in the same or a similar locality under the same or similar circumstances. This is the sole standard by which Architect's services are measured, and Architect makes no warranty or guarantee, express or implied, with respect to its services.

7. INSTRUMENTS OF SERVICE

7.1 Ownership. Architect and its consultants retain all common law, statutory, and other reserved rights, including copyright, in the Instruments of Service.

7.2 License. Architect grants Owner a nonexclusive, irrevocable license to use the Instruments of Service to construct, use, maintain, alter, and add to the Project, conditioned on Owner's payment of the amounts then due. The license survives termination of this Agreement, except that if Owner terminates this Agreement for convenience under Section 10.2 the license is conditioned on Owner's payment of the fees earned through the date of termination.

7.3 Use on Another Project. Owner may not use the Instruments of Service on any other project without Architect's written consent. If Owner uses the Instruments of Service without retaining Architect, Owner does so at Owner's sole risk, and Owner shall indemnify Architect from any claim arising out of that use.

8. INSURANCE

Architect shall maintain, throughout the term and for three (3) years after final completion: commercial general liability insurance of $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 aggregate; automobile liability of $1,000,000; workers' compensation at statutory limits and employer's liability of $1,000,000; and professional liability insurance of $3,000,000 per claim and in the aggregate. Architect shall furnish certificates of insurance to Owner on request and shall give Owner thirty (30) days' written notice of cancellation.

9. INDEMNIFICATION AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

9.1 Indemnity. To the fullest extent permitted by law, Architect shall indemnify and hold harmless Owner and its officers, directors, and employees from and against claims, damages, losses, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions of Architect or of anyone for whose acts Architect is liable.

9.2 Limitation. The total aggregate liability of Architect to Owner arising out of this Agreement, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, shall not exceed the greater of $1,240,000 or the amount of professional liability insurance proceeds actually available for the claim. This limitation does not apply to Architect's fraud, willful misconduct, or liability that may not be limited under Pennsylvania law.

9.3 Consequential Damages. Neither Party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, punitive, or exemplary damages, or for lost profits, revenue, or use, arising out of this Agreement. This waiver does not apply to amounts a Party is required to pay a third party under Section 9.1.

10. TERM AND TERMINATION

10.1 Term. This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues until Architect completes Construction Administration, unless terminated earlier.

10.2 Termination for Convenience. Owner may terminate this Agreement for convenience on fourteen (14) days' written notice. On such a termination Owner shall pay Architect for services performed and reimbursable expenses incurred through the date of termination, plus a termination expense of five percent (5%) of the fees for services not yet performed.

10.3 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate this Agreement on seven (7) days' written notice if the other Party materially breaches and fails to cure within that period. Architect may suspend services on seven (7) days' written notice if Owner fails to pay an undisputed invoice when due, and is not in breach for doing so.

11. DISPUTE RESOLUTION

The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute arising out of this Agreement by direct negotiation between senior representatives, and then by nonbinding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Construction Industry Mediation Procedures. Mediation is a condition precedent to litigation. If mediation does not resolve the dispute within sixty (60) days after a request to mediate, either Party may commence litigation.

12. GENERAL

12.1 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

12.2 Venue. The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania.

12.3 Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, except that Owner may assign to a lender providing financing for the Project.

12.4 Notices. Notices must be in writing and are effective on delivery, when sent to the addresses first written above, with a copy to each Party's counsel.

12.5 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with Exhibit A, is the entire agreement between the Parties as to its subject matter and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, written or oral. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both Parties.

12.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

12.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original, and delivered by electronic means.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
